data.name: CompatibilityWarningText
data.value:
Here you can find advanced compatibility options. These options can solve compatibility problems or make the game faster as well as make the game unstable or not functional.
Empire Earth is an old game and although it requires very little performance, it will run poorly on many computers, especially laptops.
However you should be able to solve many problems with these options, but finding the right combination of settings can take some time.
data.comment: Warning shown before the compatibility options; the box has room for about 14 lines of 50 characters.

data.name: CompatibilityWarningConfirm
data.comment: Button that closes the compatibility warning.

data.name: InstallationStateOk
data.comment: State of an installation: its programs are there.

data.name: InstallationStateDamaged
data.comment: State of an installation: a program is missing (often deleted by an antivirus); at most about 12 characters.

data.name: InstallationStateFolderMissing
data.comment: State of an installation: the chosen folder does not exist; at most about 12 characters.

data.name: InstallationMissingProgramsFormat
data.comment: Tooltip of a damaged installation. {0}: the missing programs, e.g. Empire Earth.exe.

data.name: InstallationDamagedFormat
data.value: {0} is missing in {1}. Antivirus programs often delete or quarantine game files: restore it from the quarantine, or repair the installation with its setup.
data.comment: Hint below the list when the selected installation is damaged. {0}: the missing programs, {1}: their folder.

data.name: InstallationsSharedSettingsFormat
data.value: {0} installations of {1} use the same game settings ({2}): the settings, including the game folder stored there, are the same for all of them.
data.comment: Hint below the list when several installations share one game settings key. {0}: number of installations, {1}: Empire Earth or NeoEE, {2}: registry key.

data.name: InstallationSharedRootFormat
data.value: Empire Earth and NeoEE are installed in the same folder ({0}). The launcher uses {1}, which was installed last; uninstalling one of them also removes files of the other.
data.comment: Hint below the list (contract O11). {0}: the folder, {1}: Empire Earth or NeoEE.

data.name: InstallationNewerSetupFormat
data.value: {0} was installed by a newer setup than this launcher knows. Please update the launcher.
data.comment: Hint below the list (contract 5). {0}: the install folder.

data.name: GameSettingsDefaultsHeading
data.comment: Heading on the Game settings page above the state of the recommended settings; at most about 30 characters.

data.name: GameSettingsInstallationFormat
data.comment: The installation the Game settings page shows. {0}: Empire Earth or NeoEE, {1}: the folder of Empire Earth.exe.

data.name: DefaultsStatusAppliedFormat
data.value: {0}: the recommended settings are set up for your Windows account.
data.comment: State of the defaults of a game. {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest.

data.name: DefaultsStatusAppliedByNewerFormat
data.value: {0}: set up by a newer launcher or setup; the launcher leaves them as they are.
data.comment: State of the defaults of a game. {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest.

data.name: DefaultsStatusPendingFormat
data.value: {0}: the recommended settings are not set up for your Windows account yet.
data.comment: State of the defaults of a game. {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest.

data.name: DefaultsStatusWaitingForPlayFormat
data.value: {0}: not set up yet, because several installations share these settings. "Reset game settings" sets them up for this installation.
data.comment: State of the defaults of a game. {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest. Name the button ResetGameSettingsButton exactly.

data.name: DefaultsStatusNewerContractFormat
data.value: {0}: installed by a newer setup than this launcher knows. The launcher changes no settings; please update it.
data.comment: State of the defaults of a game (contract 5). {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest.

data.name: BlockedBySetupFormat
data.value: Not possible while the {0} setup is running.
data.comment: A change was refused because a setup runs. {0}: Empire Earth or NeoEE.

data.name: BlockedByGameFormat
data.comment: A change was refused because a game runs. {0}: the program, Empire Earth.exe or EE-AOC.exe.

data.name: DisplayQuestionFormat
data.value: Your display settings differ from the recommended ones: {0}. Apply the recommended display settings? Your current values are saved as a .reg file first.
data.comment: The question of the first run (Play page and Game settings page). {0}: the differing values, see DisplayDifferenceFormat.

data.name: DisplayDifferenceFormat
data.comment: One differing value in DisplayQuestionFormat. {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest, {1}: the value name (not translated, e.g. Game Bit Depth), {2}: the current value, {3}: the recommended value.

data.name: DisplayQuestionApply
data.comment: Button of the display question; at most about 14 characters.

data.name: DisplayQuestionKeep
data.comment: Button of the display question: keep the current display settings; at most about 14 characters.

data.name: ApplyDisplayButton
data.comment: Button on the Game settings page: writes the recommended display values (with a backup); at most about 30 characters.

data.name: ResetGameSettingsButton
data.comment: Button on the Game settings page; at most about 30 characters.

data.name: ResetConfirmFormat
data.value:
Set the settings of {0} back to the recommended values for your Windows account?
Your current settings are saved first as .reg files in {1}; double-click such a file to restore them. Player names and other values of the game stay as they are.
data.comment: Confirmation of the reset. {0}: Empire Earth and/or The Art of Conquest, {1}: the backup folder.

data.name: ResultDoneFormat
data.value: Done. Your previous settings are saved in: {0}
data.comment: Result of the reset or of the display settings. {0}: the backup folder.

data.name: ResultDone
data.comment: Result of a change without a backup.

data.name: ResultBackupFailed
data.value: Nothing was changed: the backup could not be written (details in the log).
data.comment: Result when the .reg backup failed.

data.name: ResultFailedFormat
data.value: The settings could not be changed completely (details in the log). Double-click the backup to restore the previous values: {0}
data.comment: Result when a registry value could not be written after the backup. {0}: the backup folder.

data.name: ResultFailed
data.value: The settings could not be changed (details in the log).
data.comment: Result when a change failed without a backup.

data.name: ResultNewerContract
data.value: Not possible: this installation comes from a newer setup than this launcher knows. Please update the launcher.
data.comment: Result of the reset or the display settings for an installation of a newer contract (contract 5).

data.comment: Heading of the consistency hints on the Game settings page.

data.name: HintsNone
data.value: No hints: the game settings fit together.
data.comment: Shown instead of the list when there is no hint.

data.name: HintShowColumn
data.comment: Column of the list of hints: checked = the hint is shown on the Play page; at most about 14 characters.

data.name: FindingBitDepthMismatchFormat
data.value: {0}: Game Bit Depth ({1}) differs from Texture Bit Depth ({2}); the main menu can turn white and unreadable. "Apply recommended display" sets both to 32.
data.comment: Hint. {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest, {1} and {2}: numbers of bits. Value names are not translated; name the button ApplyDisplayButton exactly.

data.name: FindingSixteenBitFormat
data.value: {0}: 16-bit colors often freeze the game on Windows 8 and later. "Apply recommended display" sets 32 bit; hide the hint if 16 bit works for you.
data.comment: Hint. {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest.

data.name: FindingRasterizerFormat
data.value: {0}: the renderer is "{1}"; recommended for this installation is "{2}". Hide the hint if you chose it on purpose.
data.comment: Hint. {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest, {1} and {2}: names of renderers (not translated).

data.name: FindingWindowLargerFormat
data.value: {0}: the game window ({1}) is larger than the screen as the game sees it ({2}). "Apply recommended display" sets {3}.
data.comment: Hint. {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest, {1}, {2}, {3}: sizes like 1920x1080.

data.name: FindingWindowHighDpiFormat
data.value: {0}: the game window ({1}) fits the screen only with the compatibility option HIGHDPIAWARE; without it, the game sees {2} at this scaling. Switch the option on below or set the Windows scaling to 100 %.
data.comment: Hint (contract O4). {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest, {1} and {2}: sizes like 1920x1080.

data.name: FindingScreenTooLowFormat
data.value: The screen is only {0} pixels high; the menus of the game need at least 768. Some menus may not fit.
data.comment: Hint (R13). {0}: the height of the screen in pixels.

data.name: FindingNotOnADriveFormat
data.value: {0}: the folder {1} is not on a drive letter, so the "Installed From" values cannot point to it. Connect the network folder as a drive, e.g. Z:.
data.comment: Hint (contract 3.3). {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest, {1}: the folder.

data.name: CompatibilityDwmOption

data.name: CompatibilityHighDpiOption

data.name: CompatibilityWindows7Option

data.name: CompatibilityAppliesToFormat

data.name: CompatibilityAllUsersFormat
data.value: Set by the setup for all users (only the setup changes it): {0}
data.comment: The read-only HKLM value of a program. {0}: program and value, e.g. EE-AOC.exe: ~ HIGHDPIAWARE.

data.name: CompatibilityVersionModeSet
data.value: A Windows compatibility mode is already set, so no second one is offered. If the setup set it for all users, a custom run of the setup without "Enable earlier Windows compatibility mode" removes it.
data.comment: Below the compatibility options (ADR 0015). The quoted text is the task of the setup (messages.iss, TaskCompatibilityWindows) and must match it.

data.name: CompatibilityNotOffered
data.value: On Windows 7 and under Wine the launcher offers no compatibility options. On Windows 7 the current setup can set them if you choose them during the installation.
data.comment: Instead of the compatibility options on Windows 7 and Wine (contract 3.7).

data.name: CompatibilityLegacyFormat
data.value: Compatibility values of an older setup ({0}), which can cause black screens on Windows 7. Run the current community setup: it removes them.
data.comment: Windows 7: old values shown read-only (contract 3.7). {0}: program and value.

data.name: RemoveRunAsAdminButton
data.comment: Button; at most about 40 characters.

data.name: CompatibilityRunAsAdminHint
data.value: An older setup set "Run as administrator" for your account (~ RUNASADMIN). The online lobby should not run as administrator.
data.comment: Above the button RemoveRunAsAdminButton.

data.name: HighDpiOffConfirmFormat
data.value: The screen is scaled to {0} %. Without HIGHDPIAWARE the game sees a smaller screen, and its window may no longer fit. Switch the option off anyway?
data.comment: Question before switching HIGHDPIAWARE off (ADR 0011). {0}: the scaling in percent.

data.name: HintBarMoreFormat

data.name: ResetConfirmButton

data.name: HighDpiOffConfirmButton

data.name: FindingFolderNotAnsiFormat
data.value: {0}: the folder {1} contains characters that Windows does not have for non-Unicode programs such as the game, so the game may not find its files. If it does not start, copy it to a folder whose name has only the letters A to Z and digits.
data.comment: Hint (ADR 0015, forum test case 20): the game folder has characters outside the ANSI code page. {0}: Empire Earth or The Art of Conquest, {1}: the folder.

data.name: LauncherAlreadyRunning
data.value: Empire Earth Launcher is already running. Please use the open window (it may be minimized or behind other windows).
data.comment: Message when the launcher is started a second time in the same Windows session (ADR 0010); the second launcher ends after it.
